title: A Flame for a True Thing
story: In the hill town of Bramble, a glass lantern woke at dusk only after someone had told it one true thing that day. Lila's lantern stayed dark on the evening of the harvest fair, even though she had talked for hours. She sat on the step and tried again, with an admission that she had pretended to like a song she actually disliked. The lantern flickered and then held a steady flame. Her cousin, waiting in the lane, heard her and laughed instead of taking offence. They took the lantern to the fair. At a stall, a man said his lantern had refused him all week. Lila offered no trick. She said the glass answered honesty, including the uncomfortable kind, and that a boast had never worked for her. He spoke about a mistake at work, and his lantern woke. The fair went on under many flames, each one tied to a truth.

vocabulary.definition: The time when daylight is fading.
A statement in which you admit the truth.
Hurt feelings caused by what someone said or did.
The practice of telling the truth.

quiz.question: When does a lantern in this town light?
options: At the fading of day, after one true statement
At dawn, after a proud speech
Only at the harvest fair, and only for cousins
Whenever a person has talked for several hours
quiz.correctAnswer: At the fading of day, after one true statement
quiz.explanation: A lantern woke at dusk only after someone had told it one true thing that day.
quiz.supportingSentence: In the hill town of Bramble, a glass lantern woke at dusk only after someone had told it one true thing that day.

quiz.question: What truth did Lila tell on the step?
options: She had pretended to enjoy a song she did not like
She had refused to attend the harvest fair
She had broken her cousin's lantern
She had not spoken to anyone all day
quiz.correctAnswer: She had pretended to enjoy a song she did not like
quiz.explanation: Her admission was that she had pretended to like a song she actually disliked.
quiz.supportingSentence: She sat on the step and tried again, with an admission that she had pretended to like a song she actually disliked.

quiz.question: What does Lila's dark lantern show at the start of the evening?
options: A long conversation was not enough to light it
The fair had banned every lantern in town
Her cousin had already taken the flame
Proud talk was the only thing the glass accepted
quiz.correctAnswer: A long conversation was not enough to light it
quiz.explanation: The lantern stayed dark even though she had talked for hours, so plenty of talk was not enough.
quiz.supportingSentence: Lila's lantern stayed dark on the evening of the harvest fair, even though she had talked for hours.

quiz.question: What does the cousin's reaction show about their relationship?
options: The awkward truth did not cause a quarrel between them
He was angry and refused to go any further
He had not heard what she admitted
He wanted her to speak proudly about the song
quiz.correctAnswer: The awkward truth did not cause a quarrel between them
quiz.explanation: He heard her and laughed instead of taking offence, so the truth did not start a quarrel.
quiz.supportingSentence: Her cousin, waiting in the lane, heard her and laughed instead of taking offence.

quiz.question: What does boast mean in this story?
options: Proud talk, rather than a plain truth
A small steady flame in glass
A quiet statement about a mistake
The hour when daylight fades
quiz.correctAnswer: Proud talk, rather than a plain truth
quiz.explanation: Lila says a boast had never worked, unlike honesty, so a boast is proud talk rather than a plain truth.
quiz.supportingSentence: She said the glass answered honesty, including the uncomfortable kind, and that a boast had never worked for her.
